title: New Application Onboarding
objective: Onboard a new application to the AWS Federated cloud platform.

destination.title: Application is ready for standard cloud deployment.

steps.title: Create SailPoint / EntraID groups for AWS onboarding

spans.text: AWS Federated Landing Zone is a self-service model: application teams own their accounts and manage their own infrastructure. Start onboarding by requesting the EntraID / SailPoint groups for the app. Who: App IT manager, Senior manager, or Business SME. Dependency: an approved app code.

blocks.text: Create EntraID groups for AWS onboarding

spans.text: Open the onboarding template -
Create a new component (Backstage) - aws-onboarding
In the Application Codes section, use the dropdown of applications where you are IT manager, IT senior manager, or business SME. Select the app code you are onboarding and click REVIEW.
Review the app code and click CREATE to submit the request.
Allow a few minutes to process, then use the displayed request numbers to complete the group-creation approvals in SailPoint.

blocks.alt: aws-onboarding Backstage template - Application Codes selection

spans.text: Manual fallback (bulk request). If the automation does not work, submit a bulk request from SailPoint:
Log in to SailPoint, click the hamburger icon, and select Batch Request -> Batch Entitlement Create.
Click Add New Batch Entitlement Request.
Click Download EntraID Template to download a spreadsheet (usable for all Harness, TFE, and AWS group creation).
Fill in and upload the spreadsheet, then submit the request.

spans.text: Once the groups are created, raise group-mapping RITM requests for Harness, AWS, and TFE. Follow the process during business days.
Open
Create a new component (Backstage) - aws-onboarding-servicenow
to open the Harness and AWS group-mapping requests, then follow the same steps as the aws-onboarding template to create the RITM tickets to the IDAM team.
Email
idam-ops@example.com
with the ticket ID, application name, security group names, and app-owner approval.
Harness group mapping - assign the RITM to the IDAM operations group and request the Azure AD SSO update for the Harness production connection to include:
SSO_DEVOPS_<App Code>_Developer, _DevLead, _DevMgr, _SQA, _OPS
SSO_DEVOPS_<App Code>_SecretMgr, _Viewer, _Harness_Viewer, _SRE
AWS group mapping - request the SSO_AWS_<App Code>_<ENV>_READONLY and _VIEWONLY groups (DEV / UAT / PROD) be mapped to the AWS SSO application.
TFE group mapping - add SSO_TFE_PROD_<APP_CODE>_PRJ_VIEWER and _PRJ_OPERATOR to Entra for the Terraform Enterprise production application (<app_code> is your project/application code, e.g. APP1).

tasks.title: Raise the Harness / AWS / TFE group-mapping RITM

spans.text: Create the Harness EntraID groups (done for you by the SailPoint automation), integrate SCIM, then validate or create the Harness org and project. The DevOps groups and their access:
Group
Access
SSO_DEVOPS_<app code>_Developer
Git PR approver; create/edit Harness services; pipeline creator/executor; org-level templates.
SSO_DEVOPS_<app code>_DevLead
Git PR approver; delete services/pipelines; pipeline approval; connectors and variables.
SSO_DEVOPS_<app code>_DevMgr
Delete environments, templates, variables, connectors at org level; pipeline approval.
SSO_DEVOPS_<app code>_SQA
View all org resources; UAT deployment approval.
SSO_DEVOPS_<app code>_OPS
View all org resources; PROD deployment approval.
SSO_DEVOPS_<app code>_SecretMgr
Set up org secrets in Harness Secrets.
SSO_DEVOPS_<app code>_Viewer
Read-only across DevOps tools + Harness; needed for container-vulnerability views.
SSO_DEVOPS_<app code>_Harness_Viewer
View all Harness resources for the org; not other DevOps tools like the Viewer role.
SSO_DEVOPS_<app code>_SRE
Replicates SRE (OPS + SRE) function; PROD & BUAT only.

SCIM integration is raised for you if you ran the group-mapping automation. To do it manually, email the IDAM operations team with the ticket ID (assign to the IDAM operations group) to sync the EntraID groups with Harness.
Validate the Harness org exists; if not, create it -
How to create a new ORG
Create the Harness project, Git repo, and Artifactory repo if they do not exist -
How to create a new project
Before launching an ECS service, confirm its infrastructure and application repositories and Harness project. Reuse existing resources, or create missing ones with the self-service pipeline.

Each service needs two separate Git repositories - one for AWS infrastructure (Terraform) and one for application/service source code - plus its own Harness App project. The Infra Harness project is shared by all services; applications with multiple microservices set up a separate App project per service.
Resource
Convention
Example
Infra code repo

APP_ws_aws_infra

{Git_Org}_{IDENTIFIER}

TFE workspace
{Git_Org}_ws_aws_{WORKSPACE_Description}
APP_ws_aws_infra
The Harness project MUST have the same name as the Git repository.
Application Artifactory repository must be of Docker type; the infrastructure Artifactory repository can be of General type.
To create the GitHub repository, Artifactory repository, and Harness project, run the Harness self-service pipeline
Create_Github_Harness_Artifactory_Repo

spans.text: Create the EntraID groups for AWS console access (created for you by the SailPoint automation), then map them to AWS via SCIM. App teams get read-only and view-only birthright access to the console.

Access

spans.text: With the AWS account provisioned, wire an org-level AWS connector in Harness so deployments can reach the account. This is a one-time setup per AWS account, not per service. See
Task 2: Creating AWS Connector using OIDC
for the full walkthrough. Skip this step if a connector already exists for the org.
Create an OIDC connector for every AWS account (DEV / UAT / BUAT / PROD).
The test region must match the deploy region (e.g. deploy to us-east-1 -> test region us-east-1).
Connect through the Harness Delegate and pick the delegate for your region: us-east-1 -> awsf-use1-cd-delegate; ca-central-1 -> awsf-cac1-cd-delegate.
The AWS Backoff Strategy step can be skipped.

title: Launch an ECS service
objective: Stand up a new ECS Fargate service and reach a first DEV deployment.

spans.text: Deployments in AWS Federated use Terraform Enterprise (TFE) for infrastructure-as-code and Harness for CI/CD, following Enterprise standards. The platform team publishes hardened L1 modules; application teams extend them into L2 code that deploys their own infrastructure.

This journey creates the infrastructure PR first. After its Harness-managed Terraform run succeeds, the generated application files are refreshed with the real outputs and submitted as a separate application PR.
Browse the published L1 modules in the
TFE Private Module Registry
Reference the
app/app_terraform-l2-examples
repository for L2 implementations of the service stack.
After the infrastructure run succeeds and the application PR is merged, run the self-service pipeline
Create_Harness_Resources_For_AWS

once per ECS service to create the Harness environment, file store, service overrides, and deployment pipeline. The journey resolves the Cluster Name, Service Name, and ECR Repository from the merged application configuration before running it.
Parameter
Description
Example
project_name
Existing Harness project name - ${lower_3letter_app_code}_${app_specific_name}.
app_ui_service
environment_name
Target environment - ${account_name}_{env_name}.
app_wkl_001_dev
environment_class
Environment class. Supported: DEV, UAT, BUAT, PROD.
DEV/UAT/PROD/BUAT
infrastructure_name
Deployment resource (ecs_cluster) in the AWS account - ${region_name}_{cluster_name}.
use1_csm-cluster
service_name
Service name to deploy in the AWS ECS cluster.
ui-service
aws_connector_id
AWS OIDC connector ID (created during onboarding) - org.{connector_id}.
org.appdevuselconnector
target_cluster
ECS cluster name in the AWS account (intended name if not yet provisioned).
csm-cluster
aws_vars_file_path
Location of the task-definition file in the app-code repo.
ecs_task-definition/dev.yaml
ecr_repository_name
ECR repository for the ECS service image - ${artifactory-docker-repo-name}/{image-name}.
app_ui_service-docker-deploy/ui-service
Set the self-service pipeline branch to Release.
The ECS Cluster Name is case-sensitive.
The AWS OIDC connector for this account is created during onboarding - reference it here (one per account: DEV / UAT / BUAT / PROD).

Once complete, the pipeline creates the Service, Overrides, Environment, File Store files, and the ECS Deployment Pipeline under the application Harness project (confirm under Project Setting -> File Store / Overrides / Environment and Project -> Pipelines).
Manual alternative: the self-service pipeline automates what Tasks 4-6 describe by hand (Harness Service, Environment/Infrastructure, Service Overrides). Use one path or the other, not both -
Task 4
Task 5
Task 6

For multiple isolated QA environments in the same account/class (e.g. DEV-QA1, DEV-QA2), run Create_Harness_Resources_For_AWS separately per environment with a unique infrastructure_name and environment_name.

tasks.title: Generate the infrastructure files and open the infrastructure PR

spans.text: Set up a pipeline in the infrastructure Harness project to provision the shared AWS resources: ECS cluster, Load Balancer (ALB), ECR repository, CloudWatch log group, IAM roles, and supporting network inputs. The application deployment run handles the ECS service resources after the application PR and CI build are ready.

Run the Harness infrastructure pipeline after the pull request is merged. It provisions the ECS cluster, ALB, ECR repository, CloudWatch log group, IAM roles, and supporting resources. Use the outputs from this run in the task-definition update; a link click alone does not mark the run successful.
Put the Terraform L2 code in the infra Git repository - use the
sample ecs-l2 code
Branches map to workspace environments: develop -> dev, release -> uat, master -> prod (same for the tfvars layout dev/uat/prod with region-specific use1.tfvars, cac1.tfvars, global.tfvars).
Choose the Terraform module version available in TFE prod; check the module docs for the required provider version.

The AWS account has a VPC and KMS key pre-provisioned; the ECR repository, IAM roles for ECS tasks, and CloudWatch log groups must be created in the IaC process before starting the ECS deployment pipeline.
Set up the pipeline per
Create Terraform Provisioning Pipeline with Harness

, then trigger it. This infrastructure run creates the shared AWS resources: security group, ALB, ECS cluster, ACM certificate, IAM roles, CloudWatch log group, S3 bucket, and ECR repository. The later application deployment run invokes Harness and Terraform for the ECS service resources. IAM role naming: {APP_CODE}-{DEV/UAT/BUAT/PROD}-ecs-{task/task-exec}-role.

Harness has no status API - verify provisioning by reading logs: Harness console (Project -> Pipeline -> Executions) and the TFE prod UI (Workspaces -> the run -> Plan / Apply logs). Success degrades to unknown, never a fabricated done.

tasks.title: Set up and trigger the Terraform infra-provisioning pipeline

spans.text: After the infrastructure pipeline succeeds, use its actual outputs to update the task-definition file in the application repository. Bring forward the cluster, log group, task role, execution role, and other resource values returned by that run before building the application image.
Review the generated application files, then create the application PR. The Harness resources pipeline remains blocked until this PR is merged.

App teams provide only the main application container definition - not the full task definition. During execution Harness injects the standard platform sidecars (OTEL, AquaSec) and generates the final task definition dynamically. See
Task 3: Creating the YAML file for Task Definition
and the
AWS ECS task-definition parameters
Field
Description
Required
name / image
Container name and Docker image.
Yes
portMappings
containerPort, hostPort, protocol, appProtocol.
Yes
cpu / memory
CPU units and memory (MiB) reserved for the container.
Yes
taskRoleArn / executionRoleArn
IAM roles for task AWS access and for ECS to pull images / publish logs.
Yes
volumes / mountPoints
Shared storage between containers; mount to container paths.
Yes for OTEL
environment / logConfiguration
Environment variables and log driver/options.
Optional
For file-based logging with OpenTelemetry and Fluentbit, a shared volume mounted at /var/log is mandatory: the app writes logs there and the OTEL sidecar reads them and pushes to CloudWatch.
Variable
Purpose
CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_NAME
CloudWatch log group (provisioned by the infra pipeline) that OTEL pushes to.
OTEL_LOG_FILE_PATH
Path to the log file written by the app container (e.g. /var/log/application.log).
OTEL_TIMESTAMP_LAYOUT
Timestamp format in the log file; must match the log format.
OTEL_LOG_REGEX_PATTERN
Regex to parse log lines; named groups (timestamp_field, log_body, ...) required.

Wait for the infrastructure run to succeed before saving these values. If the run status is unknown, leave this step pending and verify the outputs directly; do not infer success from opening a pipeline link.

tasks.title: Review the generated application files and open the application PR

spans.text: Build the application artifact (jar, Docker image, etc.) from the application repository and publish the resulting image to the configured container registry. This CI run produces the image tag consumed by the separate ECS service deployment pipeline.
Select the application repository and the Git ref that contains the updated task definition.
Choose the repository's build method and record the resulting image tag.
Wait for the CI run to succeed before starting the ECS service deployment.
The CI run builds and publishes the application image only. It does not deploy or claim that the ECS service is ready.

tasks.title: Build and publish the application image

spans.text: Use the application deployment pipeline to promote the built image and deploy the service on the ECS cluster in the application/service Harness project. Prerequisites: the infrastructure run succeeded, the task definition was updated with its actual outputs, and the application CI run produced an image.
Create the pipeline using ECSDeployment_Pipeline_CD - select beta version 1.5.5-Beta or above - then fill the inputs and run it. See
Task 7: Create a pipeline using ECSDeployment_Pipeline_CD
Input
Description
PerformECSDeployment
Default Yes. No = image promotion (Artifactory -> ECR) only; Yes = promotion and ECS deployment.
CI codebase / Repository / Artifact Path / Tag
The repo where vars.yaml lives, Artifactory repo, image path, and image tag.
Service / Environment / Infrastructure
The service, environment, and target infrastructure created earlier.

tasks.title: Set up the ECSDeployment_Pipeline_CD application pipeline

spans.text: The application deployment run uses Harness to invoke Terraform Enterprise in the target AWS account, apply the ECS service resources, and deploy the application. Trigger it from your application's Harness pipeline after the infrastructure run and CI build succeed.
Harness exposes no status API, so a successful deployment is reported as unknown rather than a confirmed done - verify the outcome in Harness directly.

After a successful deployment, verify accessibility via Route 53 DNS: open the AWS Management Console -> Route 53 -> Hosted Zones -> the relevant hosted zone, search for your service name, copy the record value / DNS name, and open it in a browser.
